body:
Recorded as a known limit in PR #649 (#647). It was already present in #186's `(merged)` path and is tracked nowhere.

**What happens.** In stack mode, suppose an out-of-batch prerequisite's PR merges into `main` while a run is going. A later-wave dependent that builds on the run's integration line can then pass the `Depends on (merged)` gate (`merged.merged_into`, `template/src/pdca_harness/merged.py:67`; `flow._runnable`, `flow.py:681` on `fix/647-stack-holds-dependent-of-out-of-batch-unmerged-prereq`). But the line was cut before that merge, so the dependent builds without the prerequisite's change.

**Fix, one of:**
- check the gate against the line the dependent will actually build on (is the prerequisite's merge commit on it?), or
- refresh the line before a later wave when a gated prerequisite has merged since the line was cut.

Add a test where the prerequisite merges between waves.

Related: #186 (closed, introduced the gate), #623 (a reverted prerequisite passes the ancestry check).

Source: `results/issue_647/pr-description.md` "Known limits" (pdca-pdca).
title: stack mode: a Depends on (merged) prerequisite that merges mid-run lets a later-wave dependent through on a line cut before the merge
